title: Check yourself: is this link really in service?

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A client's adaptor has <keep-alive>yes</keep-alive>, the channel has TCP keep-alive switched on and a read timeout of 6 minutes, and nothing sends echoes. At 14:00 the host's authorization application freezes, while its process keeps running and reading the socket. What does the client see over the next hour?

options.text: The link stays up and purchases come back declined, since the frozen application still replies with an error code
options.says: a frozen application replies with nothing; only the host's channel, below it, still answers the empty frames

options.text: The link stays up and purchases go out and expire, since the empty frames are answered below the host application
options.says: the host's channel answers each empty frame in its own read loop, so bytes keep arriving, the read timeout rarely fires, and every request expires unanswered

options.text: The link is closed after 6 minutes and traffic stops, since the read timeout fires when purchases go unanswered
options.says: the read timeout measures silence on the socket, and the answered keep-alives keep it from being silent

options.text: The link is closed after the first keep-alive and traffic stops, since the TCP stack reports the frozen application
options.says: TCP keep-alive probes the far TCP stack, which is alive; it knows nothing about the application

origin.section: 11.2 Only an Echo Proves the Host Is Answering

questions.stem: A home-grown sign-on manager serves links P and Q from one thread. It sets a boolean for P after P's 001 is answered and clears it when it finds P's ready entry missing. One night the thread spends 30 seconds waiting on a sign-on to Q that never comes back. Meanwhile P's host restarts, and P's adaptor reconnects 8 seconds later. What happens on P?

options.text: P carries purchases on a connection nobody signed on, since the boolean was never cleared while the thread was away
options.says: the thread never saw P's ready entry missing, so the flag still says signed on about a new, unsigned connection

options.text: P carries purchases on a connection that is signed on, since the adaptor repeats the last sign-on when it reconnects
options.says: the adaptor sends no 0800 of its own; nothing in jPOS 2.1.7 signs a connection on

options.text: P is signed on again when the thread comes back, since the reconnect clears the boolean through the Space
options.says: a field in the manager is not in the Space; nothing clears it except the manager's own loop

options.text: P is signed on again when the thread comes back, since a new connection makes the old boolean expire
options.says: a field does not expire; only Space entries with a lease do, and the flag is not one

origin.section: 11.3 A Sign-On Belongs to One Connection

questions.stem: A colleague's sign-on manager writes Boolean.TRUE under <mux>.enabled after each successful sign-on. The client has one QMUX, with one <ready> name, behind a MUXPool with check-enabled, and the host accepts sign-ons and echoes normally. What do the purchases get?

options.text: Purchases are approved after the first sign-on, since the pool only checks that the entry exists
options.says: with a single ready name the pool compares the entry with the ready object by identity, not mere presence

options.text: Purchases are approved after the first sign-on, since the value matches any connection that is up
options.says: Boolean.TRUE is never the same object as the adaptor's ready Date

options.text: Nothing reaches the host and each request fails at once, since the pool rejects a member that is not enabled
options.says: with no usable member the 2.1.7 pool keeps checking until the timeout and then returns null; it does not fail at once

options.text: Nothing reaches the host and each request returns null at its timeout, since the pool finds no usable member
options.says: the identity test never holds, so the pool never hands a request to the QMUX and returns null when the timeout is spent

origin.section: 11.4 A Pool Uses a Link Only While It Is Signed On

questions.stem: A host sends its own 0800 echo every 2 minutes and drops the connection after three in a row go unanswered. The client's QMUX is configured as in unit c4, with no request listener, and the client sends its own echo every 5 minutes, which the host answers. What happens to the link?

options.text: It stays up through the day, since the client's own echoes count as answers to the host's
options.says: the host's echoes are requests with their own STANs; the client's echoes answer none of them

options.text: It stays up through the day, since the client's channel answers an 0800 by itself
options.says: the channel only answers empty keep-alive frames; an 0800 goes up to QMUX like any message

options.text: It is dropped every few minutes, since the host's echoes wait in a queue where nothing answers them
options.says: the echoes match no waiting request, no listener takes them, and they expire on the unhandled queue

options.text: It is dropped every few minutes, since QMUX sends back an error for requests it did not send
options.says: QMUX never answers on its own; an unmatched message goes to the listeners or the unhandled queue

origin.section: 11.6 The Host's Own Echo Is a Request, and Someone Must Answer It

concepts: The host's own echo matches no waiting request; without a request listener that answers it through its source, it ends on the unhandled queue and the host drops the link.
An enabled mark that is not the ready object, such as Boolean.TRUE, never matches, so the pool never uses the link.
Adaptor and TCP keep-alives are answered below the host application, so only an expired echo shows that the host stopped answering.
A sign-on belongs to the connection whose ready object it stored; comparing that object by identity catches every reconnect, while a boolean flag misses one that happened while the loop was busy.
